Wayfare is Meridian Studio's realtime departure-display program for Halcyon
Transit: platform displays for three pilot stations — Ashport Central, Ferry
Quay, Millbrook Bridge — fed by live vehicle-position data.

Scope agreed at the kickoff (2026-02-20) with Petra Lindqvist: sub-second
perceived freshness, outdoor readability, and a June ship date. The displays
speak MQTT (decision d-002) and went from per-display autonomy (d-003) to an
edge-gateway hub (d-008) after field maintenance pain. The palette is
green-and-amber for outdoor readability (d-009).

Team: Dev Okonkwo (firmware), Noor Haddad (renderer), June Park (design),
Bram Oyelaran (fleet), Katrin Ilic (QA), Theo Kanda (systems).
Shipped 2026-06-12; ship retro in m-008.

The Larkspur Archive is a digitized-collection platform for Bellweather
Books: scanning, OCR, searchable metadata, and an online viewer. The OCR
pipeline uses a remote OCR API over local OCR (decision d-004, informed by
the ocr-comparison notes); a later latency benchmark (s-006) showed archival
page scans running far below the assumed throughput, which sent Dev and
Silas back to preprocessing. The viewer is IIIF-based (decision d-011),
prototyped in s-010.

Team: Silas Brandt (data), June Park (interface), Dev Okonkwo (OCR pipeline),
Odessa Klein (user research). Rowan Ellery is the client sponsor; Quill &
Marrow advised the metadata descriptions. Mid-project review with Bellweather
is m-007.

As of mid-June the project is active: OCR continues at the corrected rate and
the IIIF viewer is in integration.

Context: Bellweather wants its digitized collections viewable and portable; a
custom gallery would lock scans to one interface.

Options considered: a custom-built gallery; an IIIF-based viewer over
standardized image and manifest APIs.

Decision: Larkspur ships an IIIF-based viewer — deep zoom, page order, and
metadata from standardized manifests — so the scans stay portable across
viewer implementations, informed by iiif-overview.

Consequences: viewer work is integration rather than invention; prototyped
in s-010 and shown at the Bellweather review (m-007).

final_answer:
Based on the records, June Park is Meridian Studio's **product designer** with contributions across two major studio projects:

## Wayfare (realtime departure displays for Halcyon Transit)
- **Designed the Wayfare display interface** and **owns its design tokens** — the green-and-amber palette chosen for outdoor readability [people/june-park.md]
- **Ran platform contrast testing with Odessa Klein** that settled the final palette — this collaboration is also noted in Odessa's record: "drove the palette contrast testing with June Park that settled the green-and-amber palette" [people/odessa-klein.md]
- Part of the shipped team (delivered 2026-06-12) alongside Dev Okonkwo (firmware), Noor Haddad (renderer), Bram Oyelaran (fleet), Katrin Ilic (QA), and Theo Kanda (systems) [projects/wayfare.md]

## Larkspur Archive (digitized collections platform for Bellweather Books)
- **Designed the Larkspur Archive's reading experience** [people/june-park.md]
- **Prototyped the IIIF viewer with Dev Okonkwo** — they built the prototype per decision d-011, implementing deep zoom on full-page spreads, page order from manifests, and metadata rendering per the Dublin Core house style [sessions/s-010.md]
- The IIIF viewer decision (d-011) was made so scans stay portable across viewer implementations, and the prototype was shown at the Bellweather review (m-007) [decisions/d-011.md]
- Part of the active project team with Silas Brandt (data), Dev Okonkwo (OCR pipeline), and Odessa Klein (user research) [projects/larkspur-archive.md]
